A plate with mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the half-ellipses $y=\sqrt{9-3{x}^{2}}$ and $y=\sqrt{3-{x}^{2}},$ and the lines $x=\pm 1.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the $x$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=1.$

A plate with mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ in the first quadrant enclosed between the curve $y=\sqrt x$ and the line $x=1,$ as shown above. 
The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the $x$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=-1.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
I_l = \iint\limits_D \lambda (x,y) [r(x,y)]^2 \:\textrm{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt x \right\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130823/assets/7faaecf39250dbdd1b92d789f6c217afe883c27533b563dae82ed82d228d9b4d.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $x=-1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y) = |x-(-1)| = |x+1|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda(x,y) = k |y| = ky,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}ky\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda(x,y) = k y = 4M y.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4My\,|x+1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4My(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+1)^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+1)^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+1)^{2}(x-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2M{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2M{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}+\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2M(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =2M\cdot \frac{17}{12} \\  & =\frac{17M}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
